ARGUMENTS 14. I have heard the Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the accused at length. I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record. 
15. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the State that all the ingredients of the offences are fulfilled in the present case. He has argued that prosecution witnesses have categorically deposed about the commission of offence and there is no ground to disbelieve their testimony. He further contends that the documentary evidence has proved the offences beyond reasonable doubt. As such, it is prayed that the accused persons be punished for the said offences. 
16. Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for the accused persons has argued that the State has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Ld. Counsel for accused further argued that the entire case of the prosecution is false and fabricated and the same is evident from the material inconsistencies and contradictions borne out from the material on record. It is argued that the prosecution has failed to discharge the burden cast upon it. As Abhinav Ahlawat FIR No.416/2014,

INGREDIENTS OF THE OFFENCE 17. The allegations levelled against accused are segregated into two parts. Firstly, that both accused persons on unknown date and time in the flat no. 239 sanskriti apartment sector 19 dwarka assaulted and wilfully neglected the child namely Raju, while they had the actual control over him and thereby committed offence punishable under section 23 Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act. Secondly, that accused persons had voluntarily caused hurt to the child namely Raju and thereby committed offence punishable under section 323 IPC.
18. Let us deal with the first set of allegations against the accused persons regarding the offence punishable under section 23 JJ Act, 2000. Before delving into the merits of case, it is apposite to delineate the ingredients of the offences for which the accused persons have been tried. 
19. It may be brought on record that in the present case, the provisions of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children Act 2000, (now repealed) are applicable as the alleged incident is of the year 2014 i.e. before the passing of the current legislation on this subject i.e. The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015. At the outset the prosecution needs to prove that the complainant was a juvenile when the complaint regarding his missing was first lodged i.e.,
21.10.2014. 
As per Section 2 clause (k) "A Juvenile or child means a person who has not completed 18 years of age". Thus, the prosecution needs to prove that the complainant had not Abhinav Digitally signed by Abhinav Ahlawat FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr. Page 14 of 23 Ahlawat 16:00:27 +0530 Date: 2024.03.01 completed the age of 18 years till 21.10.2014 i.e. the date on which the complaint regarding his missing was first lodged. Further Rule 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children), Rules 2007 is applicable to determine the age of a juvenile. 
20. During the course of investigation the certificate along with admission role regarding date of birth of child victim Raju Mehto s/o Sri Krishna Mahto Ex.A4 was procured, which is a certificate issued by then school situated in Ranchi, Jharkhand of the child mentioning his date of birth as 12.06.2003. The said certificate was admitted by both the accused persons duly admission/ denial of the documents u/s 294 Cr.PC on 27.04.2023. 
Therefore, it is clear that at the time when the complaint qua juvenile going missing was first lodged on 21.10.2014, child namely Raju was about 11 years old and was certainty a juvenile. 
21. The first set of allegations revolves around commission of offences u/S 23 Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000. The said provision is as follows;

Punishment for cruelty to juvenile or child. -- Whoever, having the actual charge of, or control over, a juvenile or the child, assaults, abandons, exposes or wilfully neglects the juvenile or causes or procures him to be assaulted, abandoned, exposed or neglected in a manner likely to cause such juvenile or the child unnecessary mental or physical suffering shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine, or with both." 
22. The words used in Section 23 Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2000, "who ever having charge/control over the juvenile", the word having charge or control assume significance as it denotes that any person having control over the juvenile will be himself liable if he fails to look Abhinav by Abhinav Ahlawat FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr. Page 15 of 23 Ahlawat Date: 2024.03.01 16:00:36 +0530 after the welfare of child by assaulting him or by neglecting him which causes the juvenile unnecessary mental or physical suffereing. 
In the present matter, it is the case of prosecution that the juvenile was brought to the house of accused persons by his aunt (Bua) upon the death / murder of the father of juvenile and thereafter accused Amit Verma allowed the juvenile to reside at his premises and agreed to take care of his educational needs. It is the prosecution case that juvenile child went away from the house of accused Amit Verma due to beating given by the accused persons. 
It is important to mention here that it was accused Amit Verma only who had moved the complaint dated 21.10.2014 to the SHO Sector-23, Dwarka regarding missing of boy namely Raju Mehto. The child was subsequently found on 31.10.2014. 
23. Ld. counsel for accused persons submits that the charge framed against the accused persons are baseless as it was the accused Amit Verma who was actually looking after the child. He stated about the following defences:
i) Prosecution never examined aunt (Bua) of child/ Mahender/ even mother of child.
ii) No medical document qua injuries as complained by the child.
iii) Child always had opportunity to complain against accused to the authorities and relatives, if any, misdeeds were done by the accused persons as he was having access to the landline phone affixed at the house of accused and the child had knowledge to use the same as he had also called his family members by using the mobile phone of Mahender with whom he started working after leaving the house of accused.
iv) It is also the defence of accused persons that they had also tried to get the child admitted in the school but the said admission FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr. Page 16 of 23 Abhinav Ahlawat Ahlawat Date:

24. The material witnesses in the present case are PW1, the complainant child Raju himself and PW3 Mahender Pal before whom the child went away after going out of the house of the accused persons and the remaining witnesses are formal in nature. 
25. PW1 child Raju stated that in year 2014-15 he met the accused Amit Verma in a family marriage and he was asked if wanted to accompany accused Amit Verma to Delhi for studies. PW1 further stated that he came to Delhi with accused Amit Verma whereafter he took him for school admission but he could not get the school admission. PW1 categorically stated that he used to reside with accused Amit Verma at his house. PW1 stated that accused Amit verma's wife that is accused Binny verma used to beat him and slap him in the absence of Amit Verma and for the same reason he ran away from their house and went to a kulcha vendor, where he remained for few days.

Every child deserves to grow up in an environment filled with love, care and support. Such neglect deprives the child not only of essential nurturing and guidance but also undermines their sense of security and self-worth. It is imperative that we as a society recognise and address instances of wilful neglect promptly and effectively.

Instances of beating were stated by the child which created a sense of fear in him which ultimately led him to leave the house. Secondly, that accused persons had voluntarily caused hurt to the child namely Raju and thereby committed offence punishable under section 323 IPC.
18.
Let us deal with the first set of allegations against the accused persons regarding the offence punishable under section 23 JJ Act, 2000.
summary.ANALYSIS:
Further Rule 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children), Rules 2007 is applicable to determine the age of a juvenile.
The said certificate was admitted by both the accused persons duly admission/ denial of the documents u/s 294 Cr.PC on 27.04.2023.

Therefore, it is clear that at the time when the complaint qua juvenile going missing was first lodged on 21.10.2014, child namely Raju was about 11 years old and was certainty a juvenile.
22. The words used in Section 23 Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2000, "who ever having charge/control over the juvenile", the word having charge or control assume significance as it denotes that any person having control over the juvenile will be himself liable if he fails to look Abhinav by Abhinav Ahlawat FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr.

In the present matter, it is the case of prosecution that the juvenile was brought to the house of accused persons by his aunt (Bua) upon the death / murder of the father of juvenile and thereafter accused Amit Verma allowed the juvenile to reside at his premises and agreed to take care of his educational needs.

Section 164 Cr.PC statements are accepted as evidence in Court proceedings.
They hold weight and can be used to establish facts in a criminal case.
Consistency between the Section 164 statement and subsequent court testimony bolsters the overall case.

Although, as stated in the testimonies, both accused persons used to make child PW1 work in the household work and never took any steps for getting the child admitted in any school by either calling the mother or chacha.

There seems to be no ulterior motive for the complainant and PW3 to depose falsely against accused persons.

Furthermore, the fact that the child used the mobile of PW3 for calling his uncle and not that of accused Amit speaks volume of the fact that child was not able to contact his family member with his free will and he had to take the drastic step of running away as he was subjected to unnecessary mental and physical suffering.
State vs Amit Verma on 1 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49156307/
12 29.
Therefore, keeping in view the mandate of the words used in Section 23 of Juvenile Justice Act,
the same are to be interpreted in its literal meaning.
In the present case, both accused persons did not lead any defence evidence but they both stated in their statements recorded under section 313 crpc that they were taking care of the child since 2013 as his father had passed away, and that they were taking care of the educational medical expenses of the child.

It is quite obvious that both the accused persons were having not only the physical control over the child but having the charge to take care over the mental well-being of the child.
The mother had sent the child to the custody of the accused persons for precisely the same reason whereupon the child had agreed to come to Delhi.
Any other interpretation would be a travesty of FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr.
Every child deserves to grow up in an environment filled with love, care and support.
Such neglect deprives the child not only of essential nurturing and guidance but also undermines their sense of security and self-worth.
It is imperative that we as a society recognise and address instances of wilful neglect promptly and effectively.

In the instant case, it is evident from the testimony of the child PW1 that he was made to do the household work although he was sent for some other purposes.
Instances of beating were stated by the child which created a sense of fear in him which ultimately led him to leave the house.
This is nothing but wilfully creating a hostile environment for child who was living without his mother in a house send for giving him a sense of comfort and security.

In these circumstances, in view of testimony of the child PW1, it is proved beyond doubt that accused persons having the actual custody of PW1 caused will neglect of him which caused mental and physical suffering to him, and accordingly, both accused persons are convicted for the offence punishable and U/s 23 Juvenile Justice Act, 2000.

In the present case, as discussed above no evidence has been brought on record by the prosecution to prove the fact that child sustained any injury on his body by the actions of the accused persons.
Apart from the testimony of the child including the statement recorded under section 164 Cr.PC, nothing was brought to substantiate the point that accused persons gave beatings to the child.
There is no MLC on record, nor any other corroborative evidence.
Although, it is the version of the child that he ran away from the house of the accused persons as he had received beatings from the accused Binny Verma by way of wiper in the absence of accused Amit Verma while he remained in their house for about one year in his examination in chief.
However, the child did not mention anything in the examination in chief regarding the date and the time when he has received those meetings.
And it was only when ld. APP sought permission for cross examining the child, wherein he mentioned further details.
As there is no MLC on record qua the alleged beatings being given to the child by accused persons the charge of section 323 IPC is not substantiated.

Accordingly, this Court is of the opinion that it is not safe to hold the accused persons liable for the beatings in the absence of convincing evidences, and thereby both accused persons are given benefit of doubt and accordingly, acquitted for the offence punishable under section 323 IPC.
Abhinav Ahlawat FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr.
The prosecution has been able to establish beyond reasonable doubts all the ingredients of section 23 of Juvenile Justice Act, 2000.
34.
In the light of above discussions, the Court is of the view that prosecution has been successful in establishing the guilt of the accused persons and accordingly accused 1. Amit Verma and 2. Binny Verma are hereby convicted for offence punishable u/s 23 Juvenile Justice Act, 2000.
